transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I came in because my mind’s been all over the place these past few months. Every CB chirp, a fuel price sign, some new idea—it pulls me off track. I’m missing details I normally wouldn’t, like a client’s delivery note or who I said I’d call back.
Would you say you've always been someone who's easily distracted, even back in school, or is this scattered feeling something new that started just in the last few months?

No, I wasn’t always like this. It’s really been these last few months. Now every little thing—the CB chirping, a fuel price sign, some idea that pops into my head—pulls me away, and I’m missing details I normally wouldn’t.
Over these past few months, have you noticed your mood feeling unusually elevated, euphoric, or irritable, along with having much more energy than usual or needing less sleep?
Yeah. I’ve been either really fired up, like everything’s going to work out no matter what, or I’m snapping at little things at home or out in the yard. That’s not usually how I am.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports an abrupt, sustained change (several months) from baseline functioning marked by elevated/expansive mood alternating with irritability, increased energy, decreased need for sleep, distractibility, and inattention leading to functional errors at work. Symptoms represent a discrete manic episode without evidence of psychotic features, prior depressive episodes, or a longstanding pattern consistent with ADHD, supporting a single manic episode (F30.0) rather than bipolar disorder (which requires evidence of a prior mood episode) or a psychotic-level mania.
